During the verification process, Wix may request further information—such as a color copy of a valid government-issued photo ID, a bank statement, an address verification document (e.g., utility bill issued within the last 6 months), and a document proving the validity/ownership of your VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN—which must be uploaded to your Wix Payments Dashboard. Wix Payments will contact you by email (using the email address used to set up your Wix account; check your spam folder) if additional information or cooperation is needed. You have 30 days from the first transaction to complete the setup/verification, or your account will be suspended.

If your Premium plan was canceled (for example, after a missed renewal/payment failure), you can simply purchase a new plan by upgrading the site again. If you are having trouble repurchasing after cancellation, unassign the canceled plan from your site and try to upgrade again. Also, if you cannot find the subscription at all, you may be looking in the wrong Wix account—use the Account Email Locator to find the correct account email associated with your site.

According to the documentation, it is not possible to restore deleted Wix Stores products. While you can view and restore previous versions of your site in the Site History section, the docs explicitly state that certain page types such as Wix Stores products cannot be restored this way. Additionally, CMS backups do not affect Wix App collections (such as Wix Stores), as they get their content from the relevant app, so restoring a CMS backup will not bring back deleted products.

To restore a selection of specific collections (projects) in your Wix CMS, use the backup restore feature: 1) Go to CMS in your site's dashboard. 2) Click More Actions at the top. 3) Click Backups. 4) Click Restore next to the backup you want to restore. 5) Click the checkbox next to each collection you want to restore. 6) Click Restore [#] Collections. 7) Click Yes, I am sure to confirm you want to permanently override changes made after the backup creation date. 8) Click Restore. Note that restoring a collection permanently deletes any changes made after the backup was created, including site visitor submissions saved after the backup date. Wix App collections (e.g., Wix Stores, Wix Bookings) are not affected by backups.

According to the Wix Payments account setup documentation, it is not possible to switch between business types once you select one. If you already selected Individual/Sole Proprietorship, you cannot change it to Partnership/LLC/Corporation/NGO within the same Wix Payments account setup. To use an EIN under the LLC/business entity type, you would need to select Partnership/LLC/Corporation/NGO during setup (which requires your legal business name, company registration number / EIN, company registration document, business bank account, etc.) rather than the Individual/Sole Proprietorship option.

To rename a menu item in the Wix Editor: For a regular menu, click 'Pages and Menu' on the left side of the Editor, hover over the relevant menu item, click the More Actions icon, and select 'Rename', then enter the new name and click Done. If you have an advanced menu, click the advanced menu in your editor, click 'Manage Menu', click the More Actions icon next to the item, click 'Rename / Rename page', enter the new name, and click Done. Note: If you change the name of a page in the menu panel, it automatically updates across your entire site.

To transfer the edited page from your copy site back to the original site, use the copy and paste feature between Wix Editor sites: 1) Open the Editor of the copy site (the one with your edits). 2) Click 'Menus & Pages' (or 'Pages & Menu') on the left side. 3) Right-click the page you want to transfer and select 'Copy'. 4) Open the Editor of your original site in the same browser. 5) Right-click anywhere on the screen and select 'Paste' (or 'Paste & Apply Site Theme' if you want to apply the original site's colors and fonts). 6) Rename the pasted page if needed and click 'Done'. Note: The pasted page is added as a main page to the site menu, and password protection/members-only settings are not preserved (password protection is removed; members-only pages become accessible to all members).

To delete a lightbox in the Wix Editor: 1) Click Pages & Menu on the left side of the editor, then click Lightboxes. 2) Click the relevant lightbox in the Pages & Menu panel. 3) Click the More Actions icon. 4) Click Delete.

If you deleted the element in your current session, click the Undo icon in the top bar of the Editor to revert the change. If you deleted it in a previous session (after closing the tab or signing out), you can restore a previous version of your site using Site History.

To connect your Instagram business account to your Wix site, you must first have a Facebook account and ensure your Instagram account is converted to a business account and connected to a Facebook page. In the Wix Editor, click Add Apps, search for the Instagram Feed app, click Add to Site, select the app, click Settings, then click Connect Business Account. Choose your profile in the Log In With Facebook pop-up, select your Instagram business account profile, select the connected Facebook page, click Next, review permissions, click Done, then click OK. In the Studio Editor, click App Market, search for the Instagram Feed app, add it to your site, select it, click Settings, then follow the same Connect Business Account steps.

It is not possible to migrate or update an existing site created in the Wix Editor to the Studio Editor. To use the new Studio Editor, you must first switch to the Wix Studio platform, then rebuild your site in the Studio Editor. Existing Wix Editor sites will remain on the Wix Editor and will not be migrated automatically.

Yes. You can hide a page from your site's menu, and your site visitors can still access it if you send them a direct link to that page. To hide a page: go to your editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side, click the More Actions icon next to the relevant page, and select Hide from menu. Note that hidden pages still appear in search engines unless you take additional steps to prevent indexing.

To duplicate your site from the dashboard: Go to your site's dashboard, click Home on the left, click the Site Actions icon, then click Duplicate Site. Enter a name for the duplicate site and click Duplicate. Changes made to the copy will not affect your live site.

According to the Wix documentation, you can use the third-party app "Blocky: IP & Country Blocker by Effective Apps" to block visitors from certain countries from accessing your site. This app allows you to block unwanted visitors by country (and IP address), and blocked visitors are automatically redirected to a page of your choice. To achieve UK-only access, you would use this app to block all countries except the United Kingdom. The app is available in the Wix App Market; for support, contact Effective Apps at support@effectify.co.

Email notifications for Wix Chat and Wix Inbox messages are automatically sent to the email address associated with your Wix account. To send these notifications to a different email address (such as a separate business email), you need to add that email as a site collaborator. Note that the new email address must have a separate Wix account. To do this: Go to Inbox in your site's dashboard, click the Settings drop-down at the top right, click Notifications, then click the Profile & team tab. Click + Invite People next to Your team, enter the business email address, and click Send Invite. The recipient must go to their email inbox, click Accept Now, log in to the Wix account associated with that email, and click Accept. The new email is automatically assigned a Back Office Manager role. Finally, click the toggle under Email notifications to turn on email notifications for this email address. Optionally, you can disable email notifications to your main account email via the Email notifications toggle if you no longer want to receive them there.

You cannot directly switch the template on an existing Wix site. Instead, you must create a new site in your account and select your new template there. Once the new site is created, you can copy and paste elements and entire pages from your old site (or save design assets to reuse), import media from the Site Files folder in your Media Manager, and transfer your Premium plan and domain to the new site. Note that some features like Site Theme, Design and Layout, Premium Apps, Contacts, Site Members, Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, and others cannot be transferred and will need to be set up again on the new site.

To add an anchor to a page in the Wix Editor: 1) Go to your editor. 2) Click Add Elements on the left side of the editor. 3) Click Menu & Anchor. 4) Click Anchor under In-Page Navigation, or drag it to the relevant location on your page. Note: It is not possible to add an anchor to your page's footer.

Since you are still in the Editor (current session), click the Undo icon in the top bar of the Editor, or press Ctrl + Z on your keyboard to revert the deletion. Note: You can only undo changes made in the current session; if you close the tab or sign out, the change cannot be undone.

Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor. If you're using the latest Editor experience, your mobile layout is automatically optimized. If you're using an earlier version, you can optimize it manually by clicking 'Page Layout Optimizer' on the left side of the mobile Editor and then clicking 'Optimize Now'. You can also adjust the mobile layout by dragging elements to different locations in the mobile Editor. Note that Wix sites are only supported on mobile devices in portrait mode (not landscape), and tablet devices display the desktop version. If the site still doesn't appear correctly, clear your browser's cache and cookies, ensure you're using a supported browser (Chrome or Safari) and OS (iOS 14+ or Android 9.0+), and check that you're viewing in portrait mode.

According to the Wix Editor documentation, Wix Pro Gallery is explicitly listed as an element that cannot be copied between sites. When you copy and paste a page containing a Wix Pro Gallery, the gallery element itself (and its images) will not transfer to the target site. This is why you see the paste option but the images do not appear and no upload option is provided for them. To resolve this, you would need to add a new gallery to the target site and upload the images manually to that site's Media Manager. Note that when pasting other elements containing media files, you should normally be prompted to choose 'Upload' or 'Don't Upload', but this does not apply to Wix Pro Gallery.

If you previously connected an Instagram account (personal or business) and are having trouble connecting your Instagram business account to your Wix site, you should clear Wix cookies from your browser before attempting to connect again. According to the troubleshooting steps, this applies both when connecting the Instagram Feed app to your site and when connecting Instagram to Wix Inbox. After clearing the cookies, try reconnecting your Instagram business account through the app settings or Inbox communication channels.

To open your browser in incognito/private browsing mode to troubleshoot Wix Editor performance issues, use these keyboard shortcuts: Chrome: Press Ctrl + Shift + N (Cmd + Shift + N on Mac). Firefox: Press Ctrl + Shift + P (Cmd + Shift + P on Mac). Safari: Press Cmd + Shift + N. Microsoft Edge: Press Ctrl + Shift + N. If the issue doesn't occur in incognito mode, it's likely a local browser problem that can be fixed with the Wix Technical Assistant.

A 404 error means the page doesn't exist on the server at the URL entered. Since this occurs across multiple platforms and users, common causes include: your site hasn't been published yet, the URL entered is incorrect, your domain isn't properly connected, the page was deleted or its URL changed, or search engine results are cached from a previously connected site. To resolve: reload the page by pressing Ctrl + F5 (or Cmd + R on a Mac), verify the URL is correct and re-enter it, try accessing the page by going to your homepage URL first and then navigating via a different link, or use another supported browser. If the problem persists, contact Wix support.

To transfer an edited page from your duplicate (copy) site back to your original site without overwriting the original page, use the copy-and-paste page feature: In the Editor of the duplicate site, click Menus & Pages on the left, right-click the edited page, and select Copy. Then open the Editor of your original site, right-click anywhere on the screen, and select Paste (or Paste & Apply Site Theme if you want the original site's colors and fonts). The pasted page is added as a new main page in the Site Menu; rename it as needed so it does not replace the original page.

This issue occurs when the image scaling setting on your strip is set to 'Tile' (which displays the image in tile formation across the available space, causing it to appear multiplied) or 'Original Size' (which may cause parts of the image to be cut off). To fix this, go to your editor, select the image on the strip, click 'Change Strip Background' (or 'Change Column Background' if it's in a column), then click 'Settings'. Scroll down to 'Scaling & Positioning', click the 'How's the image scaled?' drop-down, and select 'Scale to Fill' so the image is resized to fill the available space without tiling or cutting off. You can then select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to choose which part of the image is in focus.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve it: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact Wix support.

When you add a new page to your site, a new item is automatically added to your site menu (including horizontal menus) with the name of the page. To add a new page: Go to your editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side, click Add Page at the top of the panel, choose a template or click + Blank Page, enter the new page name, and click Done. If you rename the page in the Pages & Menu panel, it automatically updates on your site menu.

The preview picture shown when sharing your URL is called the og:image. You can change it for an individual page by clicking Pages & Menu on the left Editor menu, selecting the relevant page, clicking More Actions, selecting Social share, then clicking Upload Image to select or upload a new image, and finally clicking Add to Page and publishing your site. To set one og:image for your entire site, open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image, click Upload Image, select your image or upload a new one, click Choose File, then click Save at the top of the dashboard and publish your site. Recommended image size is 1200 x 630 pixels with a 1.91:1 aspect ratio (width 1.9x the height) to avoid cropping, and the file should not be larger than 8MB.

Yes, Wix offers 800+ pre-set website templates (designs) created by Wix designers. These templates include sample content, color themes, galleries, inner pages, and built-in business features. They are organized into categories and subcategories based on business intent for the Wix Editor, and are also available for Editor X and Studio Editor. All templates are fully customizable—you can add, rearrange, and remove content and apps, or start from a blank canvas or wireframe template if you prefer.

To change the height of a page without a footer, click your page and drag the Adjust Page Height handle at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note: This option is only available if you have chosen the No Header & Footer layout for your page. If the handle isn't moving, an element may be blocking the resize—you cannot make a page shorter if doing so would cut off an element at the bottom. Move or delete the blocking element first; if you can't find it, use the Layers panel to locate it. You can also double-click the Adjust Page Height handle to reset the height.

To add content to a repeater in the Wix Editor: 1) Select the repeater in your editor. 2) To add a new element (like text or an image), simply drag and drop it onto one item - it will automatically be added to every item to keep the design consistent. 3) You can then customize the individual elements (such as changing text or images) for each item separately. Note that some elements cannot be attached to repeater items. To add more items to the repeater: Select the repeater, click Manage Items, then click Duplicate Item at the bottom, and edit your new item as needed.

On iPads and tablets, Wix sites are cropped within the vertical gridlines of the Editor, which can cause content to be cut off on the sides of the screen. To resolve this: 1) Make sure to place your content within the vertical gridlines in your Editor. 2) Use columns which are responsive to your screen's width to fit your content within most screens. Additionally, if text appears off-screen or wraps unexpectedly, fonts may render differently on different devices; you can expand the width of your text box slightly in the Editor to give text room to widen without appearing on the next line, then publish your site and clear your browser's cache.

To adjust the height of a section in the Wix Editor: Click the section in your Editor, then click and drag the 'Adjust section height' handle at the bottom of the section to make it taller or shorter. Note: The smallest size you can make your section is 40px.

To adjust image positioning using the Editor Toolbar: First ensure the toolbar is visible by clicking Tools in the top bar and selecting the Toolbar checkbox. Click the image, then type new values next to X (horizontal) and Y (vertical) in the toolbar, pressing Enter after each. To change layer order, click the Arrange icon and select Move forward, Move backward, Bring to front, or Send to back. To align multiple images, multi-select them, click the Align icon, and choose an alignment option. Using the Layers Panel: Click Layers on the bottom left of the editor, select Header, Page, or Footer, then click the image in the list. Move it forward with Ctrl+↑ (or Ctrl+Shift+↑ to bring to front) and backward with Ctrl+↓ (or Ctrl+Shift+↓ to send to back). If the image was moved outside the viewport, hover over the Information icon and click Recenter element. You can also click and drag the image within the Layers panel to change its order.

To undo the latest change in your site design, click the Undo icon at the top of your Editor, or press Ctrl + Z on your keyboard. Note: You can only undo changes made during your current session; if you close the tab or sign out, you cannot undo that change when you reopen the Editor. To revert changes from a previous session, use Site History to restore a prior version.

To unpublish your site using the Wix Editor: 1) Open your site in the Wix Editor. 2) Select 'Site' in the top toolbar. 3) Click 'Unpublish Site'. 4) Select 'Unpublish' in the dashboard window. 5) Click 'Unpublish' in the pop-up to confirm. Note: Unpublishing does not cancel your domain or Premium plan, and you can republish at any time by clicking 'Publish' at the top right of the editor.

Since you've already followed the steps to change the title tag in the SEO Panel and published your site, the issue may be caused by custom code added to your site. According to the documentation, adding custom code can affect your browser tab title. Try removing any custom code you added to your site to see if the correct browser tab title appears. Also note that search engines will update your page's title tag the next time they crawl your site, so you may need to wait or submit your page's URL to search engines to speed up the process.

To add a button with a link in the Wix Editor: 1) Add a button by clicking Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, clicking Button, and choosing a button type (e.g., Text & Icon Buttons or Image Buttons), then click or drag it onto your page. 2) Select the button, click the Link icon, select a link type from the list (such as a site page, external web address, or document), enter or upload the relevant link destination, and click Done.

Free space on the edges of your site on larger screens typically occurs when elements are placed outside the vertical gridlines in the Wix Editor. To correct this: 1) Use the Layers panel to identify elements that are not stretched to full-width, have a width bigger than 980px, or are placed at the edge of your Editor screen (or going off the screen). 2) If the element does not have Stretch enabled, enable it. 3) If the Stretch option is not available, add a strip and place the element inside the strip. 4) For images placed outside the gridlines, add them as a strip background instead. 5) If you manually stretched a gallery to full-width, change it to a full-width gallery. Full-width elements such as strips and lines expand and shrink with the page and do not create these edge spaces, so using them whenever possible is recommended.

To change text size in the Wix Editor: Select the relevant text box, click Edit Text, optionally highlight specific words, then drag the Font size slider or enter a specific value between 6 and 999 pixels. In ADI: Click the relevant section, click Design, click Customize Section Design, select Text Settings, and drag the Size slider. To change font size site-wide in ADI: Click Design on the top bar, select Fonts, and drag the Size slider (note: this does not affect header and footer text).

To publish your site and make it live on the internet: 1) Click **Publish** at the top right of the Wix Editor. 2) (Optional) Click **View Site** to see your live site. 3) Click **Done** to return to the editor. Note that clicking Save alone won't make changes live—you must click Publish. Once published, your site is available online at your free Wix URL (siteprefix.wixsite.com/site-name) or your connected domain name.

You can edit your published site at any time. Open the Wix Editor from your site's dashboard, make your changes, and click Publish again to make the updates go live. Even after publishing, you can continue editing as much as you want, and each time you click Publish, your changes will appear instantly on your live site.

For gaps at the bottom of a desktop page in the Wix Editor, the docs cover two cases. (1) Gap between page content and footer: remove it by adjusting the page design (select a different preset design) or by adjusting the page height — click and drag the Adjust Page Height icon to get rid of the space between the content and the footer (if the page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to click the main part of the page). (2) Gap below the footer on the live site: this can happen when page content is shorter than the current page length; resolve it by changing the page background color to match the footer, adding content to lengthen the page, resizing the footer to make it longer, or checking the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap. Also, if a full-width element (line, horizontal menu, gallery) is stretched, gaps can appear around it — use Zoom out to 50% to move/delete the spaces, or manually drag the element.

For UK businesses, Wix supports the following third-party POS solutions: (1) SumUp – Wix Mobile POS with SumUp is available in the UK (alongside Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Switzerland); connect SumUp as your payment provider and order a SumUp Bluetooth card reader to accept cash or card payments on your phone. (2) Square – Wix Mobile POS with Square is available in the UK (alongside US, Canada, Japan, Australia, Ireland, and Falkland Islands); connect Square as your payment provider to turn your phone into a POS. (3) skuIQ Real-Time Inventory Sync – available in the UK, this app syncs inventory, orders, and customer data between your POS and eCommerce store, and integrates with POS systems including Clover, Square, Lightspeed, Vend, and Erply. If Wix Payments POS is not available in your area, SumUp and Square are the documented third-party alternatives for in-person transactions.

In the UK, the available Wix POS solutions are Wix Mobile POS with SumUp, Wix Mobile POS with Square, and cash payments via the Wix mobile app. Wix Payments POS is not available in the UK (it is currently only available to Canadian and U.S.-based merchants).

**1. Wix Mobile POS with SumUp (available in the UK)**
- Step 1: Download the Wix app from the Apple App Store (iPhone) or Google Play (Android).
- Step 2: Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard and connect SumUp as your payment provider. Note: You can set up SumUp without an upgrade, but to start collecting payments you'll need a Premium plan or Studio plan that supports payments.
- Step 3: Order a SumUp card reader from SumUp. SumUp card readers connect to your smartphone or tablet via Bluetooth and can be used to swipe, tap, or insert debit/credit cards.

**2. Wix Mobile POS with Square (available in the UK)**
- Step 1: Download the Wix app from the App Store (iOS) or Play Store (Android).
- Step 2: Download the Square Point of Sale (POS) app to your mobile device (search for 'Square Point of Sale (POS)' in the App Store or Play Store and tap Get/Install).
- Step 3: Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard and set up Square as your payment provider. Note: You can set up Square without an upgrade, but to start collecting payments you'll need a Premium plan or Studio plan that supports payments.
- Step 4: Order a free magstripe card reader from Square, which plugs into your smartphone or tablet's headphone jack to swipe credit cards. You can also manually enter credit card numbers (note: Square charges a higher processing fee for manual entry).

**3. Cash payments**
- Download the Wix mobile app. You are then ready to accept cash payments on your mobile device with no further setup required.

Note: The Wix Retail POS tablet solution for brick & mortar stores is referenced as a separate option, but the provided documentation does not explicitly confirm its availability in the UK.

If you are still unable to open your editor, contact Wix Customer Care and provide the following details: the name or URL of your Wix site; the name and version of the web browser you're using; the name and version of your computer's operating system; and a screenshot of your console view showing the first line of the error message. To capture the console screenshot: open an incognito window in your browser, sign in to Wix and try to open your editor, open the console (Ctrl + Shift + J on PC or Cmd + Option + J on Mac), click the Console tab at the top of the panel and refresh the page (F5), then take a screenshot of the entire browser window including the console with the first red error message(s).

If you previously verified your site with Google manually (using the meta tag method), your site is already connected to Google. You don't need to complete the 'Connect to Google' step in your SEO Setup Checklist. If that step is still marked as not completed, you can simply ignore it.

Being indexed and crawlable does not guarantee a high ranking—Google uses many factors beyond indexing (site age, backlinks, competition, location, etc.) to determine placement, so your site may appear on a later page or not at all for specific queries. To improve visibility: (1) Re-evaluate your target keywords—ask what customers would actually type and use those terms naturally in your domain, headlines, page text, and image alt text; (2) Publish fresh, high-quality content regularly (e.g., blog posts) and build backlinks from relevant, reputable sites to boost authority; (3) Remember that search engines crawl individual pages, not the whole site, so ensure each page is optimized for its own keywords; (4) Be patient—ranking high takes time and effort, and changes rarely happen within days or weeks. For more tips, check the SEO Learning Hub or consider hiring a Wix Partner from the Marketplace.

To get a printed receipt in Wix Mobile POS: 1) Set up a compatible thermal printer (Star Micronics or Epson) and pair it with your mobile device via Bluetooth, WiFi, or Ethernet through POS settings in the Wix app. 2) At the end of a sale, after processing payment, tap 'Send Receipt' and select 'Print receipt'. You can also reprint a receipt after the sale is completed by accessing it from your orders.

To update inventory for many variants at once, use the bulk edit feature for product variants. Go to Store Products in your site's dashboard, select the product with product options, and make sure the 'Manage pricing and inventory for variants' toggle is enabled. Click Edit, then select which variants to update (you can select all variants using the checkbox at the top left, filter by specific product options, or select individual variants). From the options at the top right, choose Edit Inventory, enter the inventory amount, and click Apply. Note that you can manage up to 1000 variants per product.

To completely remove the login bar and everything associated with it, you need to delete the entire Members Area (not just the login bar element). Deleting only the login bar element leaves the Member's Area app installed on your site. To delete the Members Area: In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side, hover over Members Area, click the Actions icon, then click Delete Member's Area and confirm by clicking Delete. In the Studio Editor, click Pages on the left side, hover over Members Area, click the More Actions icon, then click Delete Member's Area and confirm. This removes all member pages (including default pages like My Account and My Orders) and the login bar. Note: You can still view and manage your members in your site dashboard under the Site Members tab after deletion.

To set up a flat rate shipping fee in Wix Stores (desktop): 1) Go to the Shipping & fulfillment settings in your site's dashboard. 2) Create or select a shipping region (click Add Region to create a new one, or click an existing default rule to edit it). 3) In the 'Select how shipping is calculated' drop-down, select Flat Rate. 4) Enter a name in the Shipping Option Name field (e.g. Standard Shipping). 5) (Optional) Enter an estimated delivery time. 6) Enter the shipping rate. 7) (Optional) Check 'Offer Free Shipping when customer buys over a certain amount' and enter the amount. 8) (Optional) Click 'Add another Delivery Option' to add additional options like Express Shipping. 9) (Optional) Check 'Add a handling fee to every order' and enter the fee. 10) Click Save. Note: If you use the Wix mobile app, go to Manage > Sales > Orders > Settings icon > Set shipping, tap the region, select Flat Rate from the Shipping method drop-down, then create a delivery option and enter the rate in the Rate field.

To fix misplaced elements on your mobile site, open the mobile editor and drag elements to your chosen location. If an element is in the menu, header, or footer, use the right-click menu to move it between these sections. For overlapping elements (often caused by large text boxes with elements on top), open the desktop Editor, break the text into multiple text boxes (one per paragraph), add elements between the text boxes with space, and group the elements together to ensure alignment. For horizontally arranged elements that shift on mobile, group them together and attach them to a transparent container box. Use the Auto Space on Drag tool to automatically create even spaces between elements when placing items in gaps.

To connect elements on your dynamic item page to CMS collection fields in the Editor: Click the element (text, image, button, etc.), then click the Connect to CMS icon. For text elements, click the 'Text connects to' drop-down and select the collection field you want to display. For images, click the drop-downs under Connections to set 'Image source connects to' (select the image field), 'Alt text connects to', 'Tooltip connects to', and 'Link connects to'. For buttons (like Back, Previous, or Next), click 'Click action connects to' to choose the dataset action or dynamic page, and 'Label connects to' to display dynamic text from a field. The dynamic item page includes a built-in dataset, so you can connect directly without adding a new one. Leave elements disconnected if you want their content to remain static across all item versions. Click Preview to test each version, then Publish when ready.

To prevent a CMS collection item from appearing on your live site before it is completed using the Wix Editor, enable the 'Control item visibility' feature and set the item's status to 'Hidden'. In the Wix Editor, click CMS on the left side, click Your Collections, select the relevant collection, click More Actions at the top and select Collection settings. Enable the 'Control item visibility' toggle and choose 'Hidden' as the default status for new items (so new items are hidden by default), then click Save. To hide a specific item, click the Status field for that item in your collection and select 'Hidden'. Hidden items cannot be read by datasets and will not appear on your live site. When the item is ready, change its status to 'Visible'.

Check that your dataset is set to "Read" or "Read & Write" mode. If the dataset is in "Write" mode, it cannot read your collection content and therefore cannot apply sort conditions to display items alphabetically on the live site. Dataset sorts only affect the order of items on connected page elements when the dataset is able to read the collection.

If Google's URL Inspection tool shows the URL is available and can be indexed but it still isn't appearing in search results, note that search engines cannot guarantee every page will be indexed and it can take time for pages to appear after publishing. First, make sure the page is published (any changes or new pages require republishing). Check that search engines are allowed to index both your site (via SEO Settings > 'Let search engines index your site' toggle) and the specific page. Verify the page is not password protected or set to members only, as these are excluded from search results. Check for a 'noindex' robots meta tag in the page code, and check if the page has a 301 redirect (delete it if so) or a customized canonical tag (reset it to default). Ensure the page has enough content (at least 250-400 words recommended) and add internal links to other pages on your site. Check Google Search Console for any manual actions against the page. Finally, use the URL Inspection tool to click 'Request Indexing' to ask Google to crawl the page again.

To set up a table and connect it to your collection in Wix Studio: 1) Click Add Elements on the left side of the editor, click Layout Tools, then click Tables, and drag a pre-designed table onto your page. 2) Click the table element, then click the Connect to CMS icon. In the Inspector panel, choose the dataset you want to display (select an existing dataset that connects to your collection, or add a new one). 3) Click Manage Table to set up columns: reorder columns by dragging, change column names via Edit label, delete columns, or click Manage Connections to choose which collection fields connect to each column using the drop-downs under Connections. 4) Customize further using the Settings icon (clicking selects, links open in, date format), the Design tab in the Inspector panel (fill color, borders, corners, shadow, text), and the Layout icon (table height, column width, show header, row height, direction, alignment).

To add and format text in a Rich Text field in the CMS: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard (or click CMS in your editor, then click Your Collections), click the relevant collection, then click the Rich Text field for the relevant item. Enter the text you want to use and choose from the available formatting options at the top of the editor (e.g. Bold, Themes, Alignment, Link). Tip: Click the Expand icon to edit the text in a larger window. Repeat these steps for each relevant collection item. The Rich Text editor uses your site's font theme, so update your site's text theme in the Wix Editor or Studio Editor to adjust heading and paragraph styles used by the editor.

To enable or disable autoplay for a Wix Video player: Go to your editor, click the Wix Video player on your page, click Settings, click the Player tab, then click the 'Autoplay on load' toggle. Enabled means videos play automatically when the page loads; disabled means visitors must click to play. Note: Videos set to autoplay always start on mute due to browser restrictions. The Autoplay on load toggle is not available for strip and slider layouts.

To create a new website and domain with Wix: First, you can use the Wix Business Name Generator to get name ideas — enter keywords and your industry, click Generate Names, and once you pick a name you can click 'Get Free Site' to start a Wix site branded with that name. To get a custom domain, go to Domains in your Wix account, click Get a New Domain, search for your desired name and extension (e.g. .com), click Get It if available, choose a registration period (1–3 years), enter your contact info, select a Privacy & Security option (Private Registration and DNSSEC is recommended), then choose a payment method and submit the purchase. Important: to connect a purchased domain to your site you must upgrade your site to a Premium or Studio plan — selected yearly Premium or Studio plans include a free one-year domain voucher. You can also add a business email (e.g. sales@mydomain.com) via Get a Business Email after purchasing the domain.

To customize the email template for your thank you emails (or any automated email) in the new automation builder: Go to Automations in your site's dashboard and create a new automation or edit an existing one. Make sure 'Send an email' is selected as the Action, then click the 'Send an email' action in your flow to open the panel. Under 'Create an email', click 'Edit' to customize your chosen email template—you can customize existing elements, add more elements (text, images, videos), and add personalized content (dynamic values). When ready, click 'Save & Continue/Publish' at the top right, then click 'Activate' or 'Save' to save your automation. You can also use 'Switch template' to choose a different template, or 'Preview & test' to send yourself a test version.

A gap below the footer on your live site can occur if the content on your page is shorter than the current page length. To resolve this, you can: (1) Change the page background color to match your footer color so the gap appears to be part of the footer; (2) Add more content to your page to make it longer and cover most of the viewport (note: you may still see a gap on larger viewports, and a vertical scrollbar may appear on smaller viewports); (3) Resize the footer to make it longer, which can give your page extra length and cover the viewport; or (4) Check the Layers panel for hidden elements that may be causing the gap, and delete or reposition them.

To identify the Layers icon in the Wix Editor, look at the bottom left of your editor (also described as the bottom of the editor) and click 'Layers'. This opens the Layers panel, which lists all elements on your page divided into Header, Page, and Footer sections. To remove collapsible text, use the Layers panel to locate the relevant element: click Layers at the bottom left, select Header/Page/Footer as needed, find the collapsible text element in the list, and click it to select it. Once selected, you can then delete or adjust it. If the element is hidden behind another element, you can also right-click the covering element, hover over 'Overlapping Items', and select the collapsible text from there.

If you've enabled the sandbox in your CMS, each collection has two versions: a sandbox version (for testing) and a live version (what visitors see). When you replace a PDF in the collection, the change is made in the sandbox collection and stays private until you sync it to the live collection. To make the updated PDF appear on your live site: 1) Enable sandbox if not already enabled: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click More Actions at the top right, select Advanced Settings, and enable the Sandbox toggle. 2) Sync the sandbox to live: Go to the relevant collection in your editor (you should see 'Sandbox Collection' at the top), select the items you want to sync (or skip selection to sync all), click 'Sync content' at the top right, choose 'Sync all items from Sandbox to Live' or 'Sync {#} selected items from Sandbox to Live', and click Sync to confirm. Note that syncing copies all content from sandbox to live, and updated items in the sandbox will overwrite the same items in the live collection. Syncing cannot be undone.

Google Ads with Wix uses a monthly subscription model combined with ad credits and daily spend limits. You pay a monthly subscription (billed before VAT) for all campaigns, of which Wix takes a 15% fee for running and optimizing the campaign, while the remaining 85% is applied directly to your ad credit. Ad credit is the total budget available across all campaigns and is spent only on ad link clicks and CTA button clicks using a pay-per-click (PPC) model. You set a daily spend amount for each campaign from your total ad credit bucket; this amount is paid up front and optimized to be spent only on clicks. If daily spend is not fully utilized due to lack of clicks, the remainder rolls over to the next month's ad credit. You can also make one-time payments to purchase additional ad credits for specific campaigns without changing your monthly subscription. Additionally, new Google advertisers may qualify for a promotional credit (e.g., $500 USD) after spending $500 USD on ad clicks within the first 60 days, which must be used within 60 days of receipt and cannot cover subscription renewals.

If the subscription is in a grace period and recurring retries are enabled, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from the customer's existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. Alternatively, you (as the site owner) can manually retry the payment by going to Subscriptions in your dashboard, selecting the subscription in grace period, clicking Collect Payment > Submit payment, and re-entering the customer's card details.

To allow search engines to index your site: Go to your SEO Dashboard, select 'Go to SEO Settings' under Tools and settings, and make sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. Also ensure your site is published, as search engines can only index published pages. To submit your sitemap to Google: Complete the Wix SEO Setup Checklist, which automatically submits your sitemap index to Google. Alternatively, you can manually submit your sitemap by first verifying your domain ownership in Google Search Console (requires a Premium plan and a connected domain), then submitting your sitemap through Google Search Console. Note that every Wix site has a sitemap that updates automatically, and it can take some time for Google to crawl and index your site after submission.

To resolve the company verification error, ensure your company registration number (Company number / Business number / EIN / UTR) exactly matches your company's registered information. Re-enter the correct Company number in the form and upload a company registration document that proves the validity and ownership of that specific registration number (Tax ID / EIN / Registration Number). Also confirm that the Legal Business Name and the registration number entered match those associated with your business bank account. If the issue persists after 7 business days and you've verified all information is correct, contact Wix Customer Care.

For integrating a third-party payment provider like Beam, assign the **Payments Admin** role. According to the documentation, a Payments Admin has full access to set up a Wix Payments account and connect third-party payment providers, including access to personal information, tax documents, and bank details, and can connect/manage payment methods and view payments. Importantly for site safety, Payments Admins **cannot edit, delete, or duplicate your site**. Avoid assigning Admin (Co-Owner) if you want to limit broader site access, as that role also grants full access to manage, edit, and publish the site. To assign the role: go to Roles & Permissions in your site's dashboard, click Invite People, enter the developer's email, select the Payments Admin checkbox, and click Send Invite (invitations are valid for 30 days).

To resize an image in your new section: click the image, then drag the handles on the edges of the image to the size you want. To add text to the section: click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click a category (such as Text), and drag the element onto the section.

According to the documentation, menu item text should automatically sync between the Pages & Menu panel and your site menu: if you rename a page in the Pages & Menu panel, it automatically updates on your site menu, and if you rename the item on your site menu, it automatically updates the Pages & Menu panel. If the text is not updating, this may indicate a general text issue potentially caused by text theme changes or formatting issues.

To start a new website design from scratch using the Wix Editor, sign in to your Wix account and go to the Templates Page. From there, select a blank template (or a blank template with a wireframe layout) to build your site exactly how you want. Hover over your chosen template and click Edit to open it in the Wix Editor, where you can then add and customize elements to create your site.

To remove a menu from your site's header, treat it as an element and delete it in the Editor: Open the Editor, click the menu in the header to select it, then either press the Delete key on your keyboard or right-click the menu and click Delete.

Site visitors can check your calendar by viewing the calendar app displayed on your website (e.g., the Google Event Calendar app). You control what they see: in the app's Settings under the Calendars tab, select the checkboxes next to the calendars you want to be visible to site visitors, or visible but with details hidden (busy). Events marked private are not shown unless you enable the 'Show private events' toggle in the Display tab.
